root_cause.text: kmalloc_nolock_noprof() in the SLUB allocator incorrectly allowed NMI-context allocation on UP kernels, where spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, enabling reentrant acquisition of the already-held n->list_lock and slab state corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that on !CONFIG_SMP “spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held,” so “kmalloc_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter the slab allocator and acquire n->list_lock that the interrupted context is already holding,” and the fix adds `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` in `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states that on !CONFIG_SMP “spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held,” so “kmalloc_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter the slab allocator and acquire n->list_lock that the interrupted context is already holding,” and the fix adds `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` in `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent kmalloc_nolock_noprof() from running in NMI context on UP systems where spin_trylock() cannot safely detect lock contention.
intent_record.what: A new early-return check was added in kmalloc_nolock_noprof() that returns NULL when CONFIG_SMP is disabled and the caller is in NMI context, along with a comment explaining that on UP systems spin_trylock() always succeeds even when the lock is already held.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents kmalloc_nolock_noprof() from proceeding in NMI context on uniprocessor builds, avoiding unsafe lock acquisition behavior caused by spin_trylock() trivially succeeding on UP and thereby preventing incorrect lock recursion or allocator misuse in that context.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent kmalloc_nolock_noprof() from running in NMI context on UP systems where spin_trylock() cannot safely detect lock contention.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the root cause by blocking kmalloc_nolock_noprof() in NMI context on UP kernels, where spin_trylock() falsely succeeds and can lead to reentrant list_lock acquisition and SLUB corruption.

candidates.rationale: This condition restricted the NMI/hardirq rejection to PREEMPT_RT builds only. On UP non-RT kernels, it failed to block NMI-context execution of kmalloc_nolock_noprof(), enabling reentrant lock acquisition via spin_trylock() no-op behavior and resulting slab corruption.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition incorrectly limited rejection of kmalloc_nolock_noprof() in NMI/hardirq context to PREEMPT_RT builds. On UP non-RT kernels, it allowed NMI-context entry, where spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, permitting reentrant acquisition of n->list_lock and causing slab state corruption.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the relevant kmalloc_nolock_noprof() logic directly, so it is sufficient. The root cause is allowing NMI-context allocation on UP kernels when the fallback path relies on kmem_cache_node->list_lock trylock semantics that can be reentered unsafely. In this commit, kmalloc_nolock_noprof() only rejects PREEMPT_RT NMI/hardirq context: `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq())) return NULL;`. There is no general `in_nmi()` rejection for non-RT/UP kernels. The function then explicitly proceeds into the debug-cache / no-__CMPXCHG_DOUBLE path described as relying on `spin_trylock_irqsave(&n->list_lock, ...)`: `But debug caches don't use that and only rely on kmem_cache_node->list_lock, so kmalloc_nolock() can attempt to allocate from debug caches by spin_trylock_irqsave(&n->list_lock, ...)`. That means NMI context is still allowed on non-RT, including UP, matching the vulnerability condition where trylock is effectively a no-op and can reenter an already-held `n->list_lock`. No fix is present here to block NMI allocation on UP or otherwise guard against this reentrant list_lock acquisition. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and unfixed.
